**The meaning of the verses**
﴿فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِمَا وَلَمْ يُتَقَبَّلْ مِنَ الْآخَرِ قَالَ لَأَقْتُلَنَّكَ ۖ قَالَ إِنَّمَا يَتَقَبَّلُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾
And relate, O Messenger, to the Children of Israel the account of the two sons of Adam, Qabil and Habil, and it is a true account: when each of them offered a sacrifice — something by which one seeks nearness to Allah the Exalted — Allah accepted Habil's sacrifice, because he was God-fearing, and did not accept Qabil's sacrifice, because he was not God-fearing. So Qabil envied his brother and said: "I will surely kill you." Habil answered: "Allah only accepts from those who fear Him."

And Habil said, admonishing his brother: "If you stretch out your hand against me to kill me, you will not find me doing as you do. I fear Allah, the Lord of all creation."

When Qabil had killed his brother, he did not know what to do with his body. So Allah sent a crow digging a hole in the ground to bury a dead crow in it, to show Qabil how to bury his brother's body. Qabil was amazed and said: "Am I unable to do what this crow did, and so cover my brother's body?" So Qabil buried his brother, and Allah punished him with regret after he had come back a loser.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. What did each of the two brothers offer as a sacrifice to Allah? And why did Allah accept it from one of them?
2. When the farmer's heart filled with envy, what did his brother say to him? And did he answer anger with anger?
3. What do we do when we see someone else given something we love? (We wish we could have the same, without wishing it would be taken away from them, and this is allowed. Blameworthy envy is hating their blessing and wishing it would be taken away.)

**This week's exercise**
Whenever your child feels jealousy in their heart this week over a gift or a success that a brother, sister or friend has had, they say, "Ma sha Allah, O Allah, bless it for him," and congratulate them with a kind word. At the end of the week, they tell you how their heart felt afterwards.
